title: Applications Project — Start or Restart Terminal MCP via Terminals Issue #3
applicability: When developing or operating Applications project's registered @ functions and the Terminals MCP Codespace needs to be started or restarted.

execution_interface.method: Post the complete JSON request as a NEW issue comment authored by the repository owner. Issue #3 invokes .github/workflows/issue-3-comment-listener.yml and executes whatPrompt on the GitHub Actions runner. The runner is not the Codespace.
execution_interface.invocation_identity: Use a distinct forWhom on every call in the form <model>_<10-digit zero-padded prime>-<task>-Applications.

codespace.relationship: Starting the Codespace initiates its configured startup behavior, including launching the Terminal MCP service. No independent MCP process-restart command is required for the start operation.

start.purpose: Start the Terminals Codespace when stopped without modifying its files or rebuilding it.

alternative_existing_workflow.whatPrompt: gh workflow run codespace-mcp-watchdog.yml --repo BestNameYet/Terminals --ref main

start.important_distinction: Dispatch acceptance is not proof the Codespace is running. The watchdog workflow starts the Codespace through the Codespaces API using its configured CODESPACE_NAME.

restart.purpose: Stop an already running Codespace and start that SAME Codespace again, allowing its startup configuration to launch Terminal MCP.
restart.step_2_wait_for_stopped_state: Confirm that the Codespace status is ShutDown (or the documented stopped status) before starting it. A stop API success response alone does not establish shutdown completion. Inspect state with the Issue #3 command: gh api 'user/codespaces/shiny-robot-v64x5jj4v4q2x96' --jq '.state'.
restart.sequence_requirement: Do not issue stop when the user only requests start. Do not submit start until the stop operation has reached its stopped state. Use a fresh forWhom for each status check and state-changing command.

update_surfaces_imperative.title: Direct update of the Terminal MCP injected imperative resource
update_surfaces_imperative.applicability: When the Applications user requests an addition, in-place revision, or expressly authorized replacement of the Terminal MCP hot-context instructions stored at BestNameYet/Surfaces/references/imperative.json on main.

authoritative_target.exclusions: Do not write BestNameYet/Terminals/references/imperatives.json, use the plural filename, or assume /workspaces/Terminals/references is the Surfaces source.

update_surfaces_imperative.method: Use the GitHub Contents API through an authenticated gh CLI running in the Codespace (direct Terminal MCP) or in the Terminals Issue #3 GitHub Actions runner. No filesystem path in the Terminals Codespace is assumed to map to the Surfaces repository. The GitHub API updates the authoritative Surfaces branch directly. Do not modify the file merely to inspect it.
update_surfaces_imperative.prerequisites: The command environment must have gh, jq, base64, and a GitHub credential authorized to write BestNameYet/Surfaces. If credentials do not have that access, report the actual API failure; do not assume that the Terminals repository token grants access to Surfaces.
update_surfaces_imperative.preparation: Set operation to append, replace_by_title, or replace_all as authorized. Replace the heredoc with exact user-authorized JSON. append adds one complete JSON object without changing prior entries; replace_by_title replaces exactly one existing top-level object with the same title in place; replace_all requires explicit authorization to replace the complete array. Preserve all otherwise unaffected entries and array ordering.
update_surfaces_imperative.command_lifetime: Each Terminal MCP call and each Issue #3 command execution starts a fresh shell. Include all assignments, temporary files, transformations, API calls, and verification in one whatPrompt, as the full script given by shell_program_template.
update_surfaces_imperative.shell_program_template:
set -euo pipefail
repository='BestNameYet/Surfaces'
file_path='references/imperative.json'
branch='main'
operation='replace_by_title'  # choose: append | replace_by_title | replace_all
workdir="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$workdir"' EXIT

# Replace this entire heredoc with the exact user-requested JSON:
# an object for append/replace_by_title, or the complete array for replace_all.
cat > "$workdir/payload.json" <<'IMPERATIVE_PAYLOAD'
{"title":"REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_INSTRUCTION_TITLE","applicability":"REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_SCOPE","required_behavior":"REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_INSTRUCTION"}
IMPERATIVE_PAYLOAD

gh api "repos/$repository/contents/$file_path?ref=$branch" > "$workdir/original-response.json"
original_sha="$(jq -er '.sha' "$workdir/original-response.json")"
jq -er '.content' "$workdir/original-response.json" | base64 --decode > "$workdir/before.json"
jq -e 'type=="array"' "$workdir/before.json" >/dev/null

case "$operation" in
  append)
    jq -e 'type=="object"' "$workdir/payload.json" >/dev/null
    jq -e --slurpfile item "$workdir/payload.json" '. + $item' "$workdir/before.json" > "$workdir/after.json"
    ;;
  replace_by_title)
    jq -e 'type=="object" and (.title | type=="string" and length>0)' "$workdir/payload.json" >/dev/null
    jq -e --slurpfile item "$workdir/payload.json" '
      ($item[0].title) as $target
      | if ([.[] | select(type=="object" and .title==$target)] | length) == 1
        then map(if type=="object" and .title==$target then $item[0] else . end)
        else error("Expected exactly one matching top-level title")
        end
    ' "$workdir/before.json" > "$workdir/after.json"
    ;;
  replace_all)
    jq -e 'type=="array"' "$workdir/payload.json" > "$workdir/after.json"
    ;;
  *) printf 'Unsupported operation: %s\n' "$operation" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

jq -e 'type=="array"' "$workdir/after.json" >/dev/null
if cmp -s "$workdir/before.json" "$workdir/after.json"; then
  printf '%s\n' 'No content change; no commit created.'
  exit 0
fi

encoded="$(base64 -w 0 "$workdir/after.json")"
jq -n --arg message "Update Surfaces imperative.json ($operation)" \
  --arg content "$encoded" --arg sha "$original_sha" --arg branch "$branch" \
  '{message:$message,content:$content,sha:$sha,branch:$branch}' > "$workdir/write-request.json"

gh api --method PUT "repos/$repository/contents/$file_path" \
  --input "$workdir/write-request.json" > "$workdir/write-result.json"

gh api "repos/$repository/contents/$file_path?ref=$branch" \
  --jq '.content' | base64 --decode > "$workdir/readback.json"

cmp "$workdir/after.json" "$workdir/readback.json"
printf 'VERIFIED commit: '
jq -er '.commit.sha' "$workdir/write-result.json"

request_template.whatPrompt: Use the complete shell_program_template after replacing the operation and heredoc payload with the user-requested edit.

issue_3.submission_format: Submit a complete JSON object as the body of a new repository-owner-authored Issue #3 comment.
issue_3.execution_location: GitHub Actions runner for .github/workflows/issue-3-comment-listener.yml. Unlike a Codespace-local file edit, the gh api operation targets the remote Surfaces repository and therefore does not require gh codespace ssh.

request_template.whatPrompt: Use the same complete shell_program_template after replacing the operation and heredoc payload with the user-requested edit; JSON-escape newlines and embedded quotes in the Issue #3 comment body.

issue_3.result_access: Read the Issue #3 output under BestNameYet/Terminals/workspaces/terminalruns/{forWhom}_{timestamp}.json and inspect the corresponding Actions execution for stderr and exit status.

update_surfaces_imperative.invocation_identity: Use a new valid forWhom on every invocation, with the documented model_prime-task-project format. The displayed IDs are examples and must not be reused.
update_surfaces_imperative.verification: The script reads the current Surfaces blob and SHA, validates the original JSON array, applies only the selected authorized transformation, writes through the Contents API with the original blob SHA, reads back Surfaces/main, and uses bytewise cmp before reporting VERIFIED with the resulting commit SHA. An API write or Issue #3 comment alone is not proof of successful readback.
update_surfaces_imperative.failure_handling: If the title is absent or duplicated, JSON invalid, GitHub API write conflicts, permissions are insufficient, or readback differs, stop and report the error without asserting verification. On a 409 conflict, fetch the new revision and reapply the authorized change against that revision instead of overwriting other changes.
update_surfaces_imperative.hot_context_note: The target is the user's hot-context source for Terminal MCP response injection. Updating Surfaces/main does not by itself prove when a running MCP server fetches or begins using the revised content; verify the relevant subsequent response separately.

verification.issue_3_execution: After each Issue #3 comment, inspect the corresponding Actions execution and the command output file under workspaces/terminalruns/{forWhom}_{timestamp}.json.
verification.codespace_state: Read Codespace state with gh api 'user/codespaces/shiny-robot-v64x5jj4v4q2x96' --jq '.state'.
verification.result_policy: A posted comment or dispatched workflow alone does not prove the Codespace started. Report actual observed state, any execution errors, and whether MCP service connectivity was independently tested.

authority_boundary: This is an Applications project reference procedure, not an automatic change to ChatGPT Project Instructions. Its Issue #3 command payload is interpreted by the live GitHub workflow; recheck the current workflow if its contract changes.
